title: Firehouse Lentil Chili
shortDescription: A thick, vegetarian chili built on lentils, beans, and fire-roasted tomatoes
subtitle: A thick, vegetarian chili built on lentils, beans, and fire-roasted tomatoes
description: Lentils, kidney beans, and fire-roasted tomatoes simmer together with chili spices into a thick, ladle-able chili. It is built for a big pot on a cold shift and holds beautifully for days.

steps.title: Build the aromatic base
steps.instruction: Heat oil in a large pot over medium. Cook onion and bell pepper 5–6 minutes until softened, then add garlic and cook 1 more minute until fragrant.

steps.title: Add lentils, tomatoes, and spices
steps.instruction: Stir in rinsed lentils, crushed tomato, chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika until everything is coated in the spiced tomato base.

steps.title: Simmer until the lentils soften
steps.instruction: Pour in vegetable broth, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a low simmer. Cook 30–35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils are tender and the chili has thickened.

steps.title: Fold in the beans
steps.instruction: Stir in kidney beans during the last 8 minutes of simmering, just long enough to heat through without breaking them down.

steps.title: Adjust seasoning and thickness
steps.instruction: Taste and add salt, more chili powder, or a splash of broth if it has gotten too thick. A good chili should hold its shape on a spoon but still pour easily from a ladle.

steps.title: Hold and set the topping bar
steps.instruction: Keep chili at a bare simmer, covered, for holding. Set cheddar and green onions out only once it's close to service so the toppings stay fresh.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover lentil chili base — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool lentil chili and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Rinse lentils well and pick through for any small stones before cooking.
Rookie tip: Resist boiling the chili hard — a gentle simmer keeps the lentils intact instead of turning to mush.
This chili freezes exceptionally well; portion it before storing for fast reheats.
Add a spoonful of cocoa powder or a square of dark chocolate for a deeper, restaurant-style chili flavor.
tonightSpread: Condiments: Shredded cheddar, sour cream, hot sauce
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool lentil chili in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Freezes well in individual portions for up to 3 months.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It is a genuine one-pot, low-cleanup dinner that happens to be vegetarian, and the lentils give it enough body and protein that it does not feel like a side dish.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: this chili is better on day two. Storage: refrigerate up to 5 days or freeze up to 3 months in portioned containers. Reheating: reheat covered on the stove with a splash of water or broth to loosen it back up.
substitutions: Use black beans or pinto beans instead of kidney beans.
Use diced sweet potato in place of half the lentils for a heartier texture.
Add ground turkey if the crew wants a hybrid, still lighter chili.
